question: What is the difference between zakat, sadaqah, fidya and kaffarah?
answer:
Our brother then says that there are so many different types of words mentioned in the Qur'an. And in reality, fidya and kaffarah and others, these are technical terms that you only need to do when you have done a particular penalty. So fidya, for example: if you are in the state of ihram and you break one of the rulings of ihram, you pay the fidya. So the fidya is not done any day of the week; it's done as a penalty. The same goes for kaffarah. Kaffarah is only done to make up a penalty. For example, if you make a qasam to Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala, and then for whatever reason you have to break the qasam, then you will pay a kaffarah. So fidya and kaffarah are both technical charities, technical sadaqahs, that you only have to give if you have done something that necessitates it. Otherwise, these are things that the average person does not need to do every day.

Our brother also says sadaqah and zakah. And the terms sadaqah and zakah, this is one of those terms that really confuses a lot of people. Let me put it to you this way, very simplistically. Sadaqah and zakah: imagine you have two Venn diagrams. What you have is that there is an overlap between these two Venn diagrams, and there's an area where sadaqah and zakah are the same. And then there is an area where zakat is separate and sadaqah is separate. So two Venn diagrams, and they're overlapping. And in the middle, sometimes when you use the term sadaqah, you mean zakat, and when you use zakat, you mean sadaqah. And there are other times when the term zakat takes on another meaning and sadaqah takes on a unique meaning.

So what does all of this mean? The Qur'an uses the terms zakat and sadaqah to imply charity for the sake of Allah. So for example, in Surah al-Tawbah, Allah says sadaqah is for eight categories of people. And Allah says, those that are constantly giving zakat. In both of these verses, Allah 'azza wa jall is using the terms zakat and sadaqah, and in reality each one of them is implying the opposite of what most people understand from these terms. And they get confused, because when you read the books of fiqh, they will say zakat is the obligatory 2.5% and sadaqah is the voluntary. And this is correct, sometimes.

Sometimes the Qur'an uses the term zakat and it means sadaqah, like for example, walladhina hum lil-zakati fa'ilun: they're constantly giving charity, any type of charity. And in Surah al-Tawbah, Allah says that sadaqah is for eight categories, and He means zakat is for eight categories.

So bottom line: the term zakat can mean, technically, that which is obligatory, but it can also mean all types of charity. And the term sadaqah technically can mean that which is not obligatory, but it can also mean that which is obligatory. How do you know all of this? By context. You go to the scholars, you go to the books of tafsir, and then you see when zakat and when sadaqah is being used, under which term. And in reality the context is very, very clear. Nobody gets confused in terms of the language of the Qur'an and Sunnah. So just keep this point in mind.

Our brother is asking what the different types are. So now you understand: **fidya and kaffarah are technical types of charity that you must give as a penalty, to make up for something that you have done.** And sadaqah and zakah, as I explained, have technical definitions, and then there's the linguistic. Technically, zakat is the obligatory amount you have to give once a year, 2.5% on the amount that you have above the nisab, and sadaqah is anything that is above that amount. And yet the Qur'an uses both of these terms for each other.
